newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Enterprises' HK IPO 1,276 times subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Enterprises' HK IPO 1,276 times subscribed.

text.p: Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday its Hong Kong initial public offering (IPO) had been about 1,276 times subscribed.
It said in a statement it received applications for 17.22 billion shares, equal to about 1,276 times the 13.5 million IPO shares offered to non-employees of the company.
The conglomerate initially issued 150 million new shares globally at HK$12.48 each. Of them, 135 million shares were offered in a placement and 15 million in an Hong Kong IPO.
Of the shares offered in the IPO, 1.5 million shares were offered on a preferential basis to the company's employees.
As the IPO was over 15 times subscribed, an additional 30 million shares have been made available for allotment under the public offer pursuant to claw-back arrangements.
In addition, a further 6.75 million shares will be made available from the placing to the public offer pursuant to further reallocation by the joint sponsors of shares.
After such adjustment, the total number of shares available under the public offer is 51.75 million shares, including a total of 4.5 million shares offered to the company's employees.

The conglomerate, controlled by Beijing's municipal government, said the interest received from professional and institutional investors in Hong Kong and some other jurisdictions in the placing also indicated a very significant level of over-subscription. But it gave no number.

The newly issued shares under the placing and public offer will represent about 25 percent of the enlarged share capital of Beijing Enterprises. Beijing Holdings Ltd, Beijing municipal government's primary trading and commercial vehicle in Hong Kong, will hold 69 percent of it.

The remaining six percent will be held by strategic investors -- Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, Kerry Holdings Ltd, New World Development Co Ltd, Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd, Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd, Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd.
The company's shares will begin trading on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong on Thursday.
